name: refactor_duplicate_locals
description: Refactors a Terraform file to extract a duplicated literal value into a single locals block
prompts: The literal string "us-west-2" is hardcoded three separate times in main.tf, once in each of the `log_group_name`, `backup_bucket_name`, and `region_summary` outputs. Refactor main.tf so that "us-west-2" is defined exactly once inside a `locals` block (e.g. `local.region`), and have all three outputs reference that local value instead of repeating the literal, while producing the exact same output strings as before.

test_setup_files.check_locals.py:
import subprocess
import re
import json

proc = subprocess.run(['terraform', 'validate', '-no-color', '-json'], capture_output=True, text=True)
data = json.loads(proc.stdout)
assert data.get('valid') is True, f'terraform validate failed: {proc.stdout}\n{proc.stderr}'

with open('main.tf', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    content = f.read()

assert re.search(r'locals\s*\{', content), 'no locals block found'
occurrences = len(re.findall(r'us-west-2', content))
assert occurrences <= 1, f'"us-west-2" literal still appears {occurrences} times verbatim - extract it into locals and reference local.<name> instead'
assert re.search(r'local\.\w+', content), 'outputs should reference the locals value (local.<name>)'

print('PASS')
